Hi Sara — great to hear from you. Quick summary below; attaching an SOW draft (Acme_SOW_v2.pdf) and a simple pricing model CSV for the examples.

High-level:
- Minimum monthly commit: We typically recommend a monthly committed spend (floor) to enable reserved capacity planning. For the initial commercial conversation we propose a $10,000/mo minimum spend for the first 12 months (billed monthly). First month is prorated if start date is mid-cycle.
- On-demand (over-commit) pricing: Excess usage above the monthly commit is billed at an "on-demand" per-token rate. Default structure is per-token on-demand = commit per-token rate * 1.4 (i.e., a 40% surcharge) to reflect burst capacity.
- Safety-net surcharge: For very short, unanticipated spikes that exceed our burst window, we have a temporary surge surcharge (an additional per-token uplift) that covers the cost of emergency capacity (applies only when sustained for >5 minutes and >300% of average QPS). This protects other customers and preserves SLAs. It is designed to be rare.
- Grace and true-up: We offer a 3-month grace period where the on-demand surcharge is phased (month 1: 20% uplift, month 2: 30%, month 3: full 40%) to ease ramp risk. Quarterly true-ups reconcile committed units with actual usage and allow credits/charges.

Examples (rounded):
- Committed rate: $0.00050 / token (equivalent to $10k @ estimated token usage profile)
- On-demand: $0.00070 / token (commit * 1.4)
- Safety-net (rare spike uplift): additional $0.00020 / token while the spike condition persists

Next steps: if Acme wants the grace/phase-in exceptions we can bake that into the SOW and limit the safety-net surcharge triggers. Ben (cc'd) can run the numbers against your projected monthly profiles.

— Tessa

Sara — following up with concrete math and a few optional concessions we can consider. Attaching redwood-pricing-model.csv for a simple token ladder.

Assumptions for the example: commit = $10,000/mo; commit per-token = $0.00050; expected monthly tokens = ~20M under normal load.

Overage math (straightforward):
- If you exceed commit by 5M tokens in a month: excess charged at $0.00070/token => extra $3,500 that month.

Safety-net behavior (operational):
- Bursts that are within our configured continuous-batching/burst window (e.g., short spikes that our runtime can absorb) are charged as on-demand only.
- If the burst exceeds operational thresholds (sustained >5 minutes and >3x baseline QPS), the safety-net surcharge kicks in for the delta only. This prevents sudden multi-customer impact.

Concessions we can offer for an enterprise first-year:
- First 3 months: on-demand uplift capped at +20% vs commit rate (not full 40%).
- Pro-rata on the initial month and a single mid-year true-up instead of quarterly (if you prefer simpler billing).

If you can share a 90-day traffic profile (peak/median tokens/day), I can run a blended estimate and show total expected monthly bill ranges under each scenario. HubSpot deal is updated here: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/ACME-2026-03

Thanks — Ben

Sara — thanks for the clear counterpoints. I manage these enterprise SOW negotiations and want to propose a pragmatic compromise that keeps both sides protected while enabling your ramp.

Proposed compromise (final commercial terms to be captured in SOW):
- Minimum monthly commit: $10,000/mo, prorated for first partial month.
- On-demand rate: commit rate + 40% (as Tessa outlined) after the commit is exhausted.
- Safety-net surcharge: will apply only above 15% month-over-month excess and is capped at 50% of the incremental on-demand uplift. We will also set the operational trigger to sustained >6 minutes and >300% baseline QPS (slightly tighter than standard to reduce false positives).
- Ramp protection: first 3 months automatically get the phase-in (20% / 30% / full 40%). This will be default Redwood behavior for new enterprise customers and does not require special approval.
- True-up cadence: we will offer annual true-up by default for this contract, with an option to switch to quarterly if you want more frequent reconciliation.

Next steps: Ben, please update the SOW with this language and route to DocuSign. Legal (cc'd) — please review the safety-net trigger and cap language for standardization. Sara — if Acme agrees, we'll send the SOW for signature and spin up an initial 90-day usage window review to calibrate thresholds.
